title: Deutsche Telekom Rises on Additional €3 Billion Share Buyback
summary: Deutsche Telekom AG’s shares surged by the most in four years after Europe’s biggest phone carrier increased its share buyback program by as much as €3 billion ($3.5 billion) in 2026 following a free-cash-flow guidance boost.

title: China’s Unitree Seeks $904 Million in First Mainland Robotic IPO
summary: China’s Yushu Technology Co., known as Unitree Robotics, is seeking to raise about 6.1 billion yuan ($904 million) in an initial public offering that would make it the mainland’s first publicly traded humanoid robot maker.

title: Leverage Shows Signs Market Is Overbought on Borrowed Money, Says Unlimited Funds CEO
summary: Bob Elliott, CEO and CIO at Unlimited Funds, discusses market FOMO in AI and chips which he sees as “classic bubble-type activity” and warns about the levels of leverage he sees across markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: WhatsApp Tests Age Confirmation in Largest Market India
summary: Meta Platforms Inc.’s WhatsApp is testing a new feature that lets users in India add their date of birth, an update to the massively popular messaging service in its largest market.

title: Peloton Gives Disappointing Outlook in Setback to Comeback Bid
summary: Peloton Interactive Inc. forecast revenue for the fiscal 2027 year that came in below estimates, marking the latest setback for the fitness technology company.

title: Snapchat Users Bristle at Plan to Charge for Memories Storage
summary: The app plans to charge users a storage fee to save their content

title: UAE Fund Weighs $6.3 Billion AI Data Center Investment in Japan
summary: The United Arab Emirates is considering investing as much as ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion) to build an artificial intelligence data center in Japan, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: Roche Uses Recursion AI to Uncover New Brain Disease Targets
summary: A new generation of AI companies believes it can reduce the number of failed drug trials.

title: SpaceX Lockup Expiration to Free $101 Billion in Stock
summary: Investors are bracing for the next potential hit to SpaceX shares when $101 billion worth of stock becomes available for trading on Thursday with the scheduled ending of a lockup agreement restricting insider share sales. Leen Al-Rashdan reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Huntington's Braddock Assesses Bank's Outlook in Texas
summary: Billy Braddock, regional group president at Huntington Bancshares Inc., discusses the bank's business in Texas after taking over Cadence Bank, the loan business in the state and the adoption of artificial intelligence. He speaks with Bloomberg's Julie Fine. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China Launches Cybersecurity Review Into Palo Alto Networks
summary: China launched a formal security review of products sold in the country by US technology firm Palo Alto Networks Inc., ramping up pressure on the company months after accusing it of harboring links to intelligence services.

title: SoftBank Secures $10 Billion Margin Loan Backed by OpenAI Stake
summary: SoftBank Group Corp. has secured a $10 billion margin loan backed by its stake in US tech giant OpenAI, marking another fundraising milestone in its bet on artificial intelligence.

title: 'Reasonable' to Allocate in US Given Earnings, Wytenus Says
summary: Erik Wytenus, EMEA head of investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, says robust earnings make it "reasonable to continue to allocate to a healthy degree to the US." He speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Siemens Disappoints Investors With Muted Outlook Raise
summary: Siemens AG disappointed investors hoping that it would show a bigger benefit from a surge in data center spending that prompted a second increase in its earnings outlook this year.

title: SoftBank Profit Beats Expectations
summary: SoftBank Group Corp. reported a smaller-than-expected decline in quarterly net income, helped by a rally in its chip-stock holdings. OpenAI’s Japanese backer is in the spotlight alongside concerns about climbing debt levels that AI service providers are taking on to spend on data centers and other infrastructure. Bloomberg's Neil Campling reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nintendo Tops Estimates With Tariff Refunds and Switch 2 Games
summary: Nintendo Co. reported stronger-than-expected earnings buoyed by tariff refunds from the US and strong sales of a pair of in-house titles for its flagship Switch 2 console.

title: OpenAI Asks Judge to Toss Apple’s Trade Secrets Lawsuit
summary: OpenAI is asking a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit filed by Apple Inc. accusing the artificial intelligence company of stealing trade secrets, saying that the iPhone maker’s allegations are meritless.

title: Siemens Is Winning Customers in China, CEO Says
summary: Siemens Chief Executive Officer Roland Busch says the company is "very competitive" in China, where the automation business is doing "very well." He also comments on the data center business. Busch speaks on Bloomberg Television after Siemens raised its earnings expectations for a second time this year due to a surge in data center spending and higher returns from selling software to industry. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Cybersecurity firm Aura CEO on 2Q26 Results
summary: Hari Ravinchandran, Founder and CEO of cyber-security platform Aura, discusses his outlook for the company's growth at it reported a 27-percent year-on-year increase in pro forma revenue. He says the firm is on track to generate positive free cash flow this year, following its acquisition of tech firm Qoria and its listing on the Australian Securities Exchange. He speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Social Media Ban: How Do Limits For Children and Teens Work?
summary: Since Australia barred under-16s from using social media in late 2025, more than two dozen countries have either enacted their own bans or are weighing similar restrictions.
